ON THE 16 th OF MAY, 2024  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 55073 of 2023  BETWEEN:-
 SHIV KUMAR PANDEY S/O LATE SHRI KESHRI PRASAD  PANDEY, AGED ABOUT 73 YEARS, OCCUPATION:
 FARMING (RETIRED ARMY OFFICER ) RESIDENT OF  VILLAGE KOSHTA KOTHAR POLICE STATION  CHURHAT DISTRICT SIDHI (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI ARUNODAYA SINGH - ADVOCATE )
 AND
1. THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH  THE STATION HOUSE OFFICER POLICE STATION  CHURHAT DISTRICT SIDHI (MADHYA PRADESH)

2 . BHAIYALAL DAHIYA (KOTWAAR) S/O SHRI  SHIVNATH KOTWAAR, AGED ABOUT 56 YEARS,
 OCCUPATION: FARMING KOSHTA KOTHAR P.S.
 AND TEH. CHURHAT DISTT. SIDHI (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI AMAN PANDEY - PANEL LAWYER)
(SHRI B.K. SHUKLA - ADVOCATE FOR RESPONDENT NO.2)

This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:
 ORDER

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail in connection with FIR/Crime No.856/0023 dated 03.10.2023 registered at Police Station Churhat, District Sidhi for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, and 120B of IPC.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is aged about 73 years.

The machinery of law in the present case has been set in motion on the allegations that after the death of one Shivnath Kotwar on 05.07.1992, a sale-deed on 20.09.1993 was shown to be executed, thus as per the prosecution the said sale-deed was a forged document.

It is contended by the counsel that factum of execution of sale-deed was well within the knowledge of the complainant which is evident from the perusal of order dated 05.12.2006 passed by the trial Court on an application moved by the complainant under Order 39 Rule 1 and 2 of CPC.
3.
It is contended by the counsel that the factum of execution of sale- deed dated 20.09.1993 was in the knowledge of the complainant since the year 2006.
However the complainant was sitting tight over the matter with oblique motive now has started prosecuting the applicant.
Thus, taking into consideration the totality of the fact as well as age of the applicant, the application for grant of anticipatory bail deserves to be allowed.
4. Per contra, the counsel for the State has opposed the prayer and submitted that in the present case the issue pertains to the execution of sale- deed in the name of a dead person.

Therefore,
considering the direct allegation, no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.

5. Heard the submissions and perused the case diary.
6.

A perusal of record prima facie reflects that the complainant was in the knowledge of the fact as regards execution of sale-deed in the year 2006 itself when an application moved under Order 39 Rule 1 and 2 of CPC was dismissed by the trial Court in a suit filed by the complainant and his brothers.

7. Thus taking into consideration the totality of the circumstances and also the age of the applicant,
this Court deems it appropriate to enlarge the applicant on anticipatory bail, therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that in the event of arrest shall be enlarged on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer for his appearance before him during the course of investigation or before the trial Court concerned during trial, as the case may be.

9. It is further directed that the applicant shall abide by all the conditions as enumerated under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C.
(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE mn Shiv Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64633339/
